baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; meta.json's root cause: PR #13495 reordered code so emptyData() runs after functions_lib_ctx is fetched via functionsLibCtxGetCurrent(); emptyData() frees/recreates the functions lib context, leaving the captured pointer dangling. Fix commit a0da8390a28a reorders to call emptyData() before fetching the pointer. No existing PoC/run.sh was provided (fast-path found none), so I inspected src/replication.c in post_intro directly: lines ~2061-2103 show the non-SWAPDB branch fetching functions_lib_ctx before the later emptyData() call at line 2090, with the pointer then passed into rdbLoadingCtx used by rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx at line 2103; src/db.c confirmed emptyData() synchronously frees the current functions lib ctx via functionsLibCtxClearCurrent(async=0)->functionsLibCtxFree when replica-lazy-flush is no (default). I crafted run.sh exercising exactly this path: a master with a loaded Lua function library syncing diskless to an on-empty-db replica. First iteration of the script backgrounded both servers and always exited 0 regardless of a child crash, which run_poc's crash-detection read as crashed=False despite an embedded ASan report in the output (record_verdict correctly rejected that evidence). I fixed the script to detect the replica dying and `wait` on its PID to propagate the real (SIGABRT-driven) exit status, re-ran all three versions with this corrected script, and confirmed: post_intro now reports exit=1 crashed=True with a clean, unambiguous AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free (READ in functionsCreateWithLibraryCtx <- rdbFunctionLoad <- rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx <- readSyncBulkPayload:2103; freed by functionsLibCtxFree <- functionsLibCtxClearCurrent <- emptyData <- readSyncBulkPayload:2090); pre_intro and post_benign both ran the identical script/config/commands and completed with exit=0 crashed=False, replica reaching full sync ('REPLICA SURVIVED / SYNCED OK'), no sanitizer report. This satisfies the same-reproducer invariance requirement and cleanly distinguishes introduction (post_intro only) from parent and companion fix.

oracle.description: Custom /poc/run.sh starts a master and replica redis-server pair (both ASan-built). Replica is configured with --repl-diskless-load on-empty-db --replica-lazy-flush no (empty db, sync flush). Master gets --repl-diskless-sync yes, a FUNCTION LOAD of a small Lua library, and a SET; then the replica issues REPLICAOF to force a full resync. The script waits for either full sync ("up") or the replica process dying, then reaps the replica's real exit status via `wait` (propagating SIGABRT from ASan as a nonzero exit) instead of masking it, so run_poc's crash detection is accurate across versions. In readSyncBulkPayload(), since repl_diskless_load != SWAPDB and the replica db is empty, use_diskless_load is true and the non-swapdb branch runs: it fetches functions_lib_ctx = functionsLibCtxGetCurrent() then (introduced ordering) calls emptyData(), which synchronously frees that same context via functionsLibCtxFree()/zfree and creates a fresh one. The stale pointer is still stored in rdbLoadingCtx and passed to rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx -> rdbFunctionLoad(), which dereferences the freed context to load the replicated function library.
